title: Spider-Verse ant short - look, craft and integrity rubric

scaling.note: Every pixel number in the research was measured at a specific resolution and has been rescaled to our 1920x803 delivery. Do not copy raw research numbers into code without applying the factor stated here.
derivations: Halftone pitch: research measured 8.0 px at 803 px picture height (= 10.7 px if scaled to 1080 p). Our picture height IS 803 px, so the target is 8.0 px unscaled. research SS1.8
Ink line width: research measured 5-6 px at 2000 px frame width. Our width is 1920 px, so 4.8-5.8 px, centred on 5.3 px. research SS3.6

Misregistration far field: research measured a 5 px three-channel spread at 803 px picture height. Our target is therefore 4.0-7.5 px, not the 6-7 px quoted for a 1080 p picture height. research SS4.2-4.3
Misregistration cap: 1 % of picture height = 8.03 px. research SS4.4

Hatch pitch: research SS2.3 gives 7-11 px as an [EST] scaled to a 1080 p picture height, which is 5.2-8.2 px at ours. The director's brief asks for a literal 7-11 px. The target below spans 6.0-11.0 px so both readings are satisfiable; aim for 7-8 px, where they overlap.

Glow / highlight screen: research SS1.8 gives 16-21 px at 1080 p picture height = 11.9-15.6 px at ours; the range below is widened to 11-22 px because the glow screen is screen-locked and art-directed per beat.

meaning.5: Load-bearing signature of the look or a hard integrity gate. If this fails the frame does not read as Spider-Verse, or the evidence cannot be trusted. All weight-5 criteria are blockers.
meaning.4: Major - a documented, measured property of the look that a viewer would name if it were missing.
meaning.3: Standard - the default for a well-defined requirement.
meaning.2: Supporting - contributes to the read but is not individually diagnostic.
meaning.1: Polish - a refinement that only matters once everything above passes.

weighting.totalFormula: score = sum(weight over passing criteria) / sum(weight over criteria with evidence); strictScore counts pending as failing.
weighting.blockerRule: Every criterion with weight 5 must pass for the rubric to report exit = true.

statuses.pending: No evidence yet - frames missing, source file not written, or a visual verdict not recorded.
statuses.error: The analyser threw. Treated as pending for scoring but reported separately.

doc.howToRead: Each row is one measurable claim about the finished 10-second short. `metric` names the number score.mjs computes; `target` and `tolerance` define the pass window; `frames` says where it is measured. Criteria marked auto are measured from the rendered PNGs alone - no self-reporting by the renderer. Criteria marked source are assertions about the code or the edit (greps, ordered pass lists, audit JSON). A handful carry visualAlso, meaning a human sign-off in verdicts.json is recorded next to the machine number but does not gate the score.
doc.howToUse: Render frames to spiderverse/out/frames, then `node spiderverse/tools/score.mjs`. Use --quick while iterating (every 8th frame), --category print to work one area, --frames 24,138,228 to interrogate a specific beat. The scorer writes spiderverse/out/score.json and spiderverse/out/score-report.md.
doc.eyeballing: To check a single still by eye, work down the categories in this order: quantisation (is it flat?), print (are the dots the right size and angle?), hatching (are the darks lines, not dots?), inkLines (are they coloured?), misregistration (is the defocus a colour offset and not a blur?), then colour, then the 2D layers. Those first five are what make a frame read as printed rather than rendered.

categories.title: Halftone / Ben-Day screen
categories.summary: One shared AM screen, object-locked on matter and screen-locked on light, applied as a multiplier around 1.0.

categories.title: Hatching
categories.summary: The shadow tier of the same Hatcher, lines instead of dots, weight carrying tone.

categories.title: Tone quantisation
categories.summary: Every smooth gradient becomes a step; every step edge becomes a screen.

categories.title: Ink lines
categories.summary: Coloured 3D curves with overshoot, taper and a held redraw interval - not a toon-shader contour.

categories.title: Misregistration as depth of field
categories.summary: Subtractive per-separation offset driven by depth. No gaussian blur anywhere.

categories.title: Motion treatment
categories.summary: Chromatic trailing along motion vectors instead of photographic motion blur.

categories.title: Frame rate and stepping
categories.summary: Character on 2s, camera on 1s, per-part rates with offset phases, and sims that respect the holds.

categories.title: Animation craft
categories.summary: Anticipation, overshoot, smears, holds, silhouettes, weight.

categories.title: Colour
categories.summary: A scripted, replaced palette rather than shaded albedo, with depth simplification.

categories.title: Lighting
categories.summary: Designed shadow shapes, halftoned rim light, graphic flares, glow dots.

criteria.title: Mid-tone halftone pitch is 8.0 px at our picture height
criteria.why: Two independent measurements (zero-padded FFT and a 569-dot nearest-neighbour histogram) agree on 8.0 px at 803 px picture height - research SS1.8.
criteria.check: Windowed 128 px tiles zero-padded to 512, high-passed, FFT; the dominant spectral peak inside a 3-40 px period annulus, refined by log-magnitude centroid, median over mid-tone tiles.

criteria.title: Lattice sits at 45 deg / 135 deg and is square
criteria.why: FFT peak bearings and nearest-neighbour bearings both land at 45 deg and 135 deg, with two equal orthogonal fundamentals - research SS1.8.
criteria.check: Primary spectral axis bearing mod 180 deg, plus the second axis found at least 20 deg away; the criterion value is the primary bearing and the detail carries the axis separation, which must be 90 +/- 8 deg.

criteria.title: Amplitude modulation - dot area tracks tone
criteria.why: "the thickness of any dot or line in a printed pattern typically reflects the brightness of that region" - US 11270474, research SS1.3. This is AM halftoning, not ordered dithering.
criteria.check: Per tile, connected-component mean dot area from the band-passed dot mask, correlated across tiles against (1 - mean luma). Pearson r.

criteria.title: Lattice pitch stays fixed while dot size varies
criteria.why: AM means a fixed lattice with a variable dot radius; if the pitch wanders with tone you have built FM dithering instead - research SS1.3.
criteria.check: Coefficient of variation of the recovered period across tiles that span the tonal range, after rejecting tiles whose spectral peak is below the RMS floor.

criteria.title: Dots merge in the darkest band
criteria.why: "in the darkest band adjacent dots merge into each other" - research SS1.3 [MEAS]. Implement coverage past 100 %.
criteria.check: Mean connected-component dot area in the darkest tone quintile divided by the mean in the middle quintile.

criteria.title: One screen shared by all three separations
criteria.why: C = 1-R, M = 1-G and Y = 1-B all measured 8.0 px at 45.0/135.0 deg on the same patch - research SS1.8 [MEAS]. The screentone is a single luminance-derived multiplier, so it physically cannot have per-ink angles.
criteria.check: Run the pitch/angle analyser independently on the three subtractive separations of the same tile; the value is the largest pairwise period difference in px.

criteria.title: No four rotated CMYK screens and no rosette
criteria.why: "Do not implement four rotated screens - you will get moire rosettes the film does not have" - research SS1.8.
criteria.check: Largest pairwise angle difference between the C, M and Y screens on the same tile. A 15/75/0/45 deg press set would show a spread near 30-45 deg.

criteria.title: The screen is a multiply, not an overlay or an over
criteria.why: "These values are then stored as a 'multiplier' layer ... the screen-tones can be applied to any image using a standard multiply" - US 11270474, research SS1.2. Compositing dots over the image gives a sticker, not a print.
criteria.check: Across tiles spanning the tonal range, regress the dot-trough value against the tile mean. A multiply passes through the origin; an over converges on a fixed ink colour. The value is the absolute intercept of the fit (detail carries slope and r-squared, which must be >= 0.7).

criteria.title: Dots are present in highlights as well as mid-tones
criteria.why: The multiplier can sit above 1.0, so dots brighten as well as darken - "that is how you get dots in highlights as well as shadows" - research SS1.2, SS1.6.
criteria.check: Band-passed modulation signal-to-noise inside the brightest tone quintile and inside the middle quintile; the value is the smaller of the two, so both bands must carry a screen.

criteria.title: Bifurcation keeps the projected pitch inside 6-24 px
criteria.why: "an optional bifurcation mode which uses derivatives to normalize the pattern scale (i.e., if the patterns became too large, then the lines or dots are split)" - US 11270474, research SS1.5, SS1.8.
criteria.check: Fraction of tiles with a valid spectral peak whose recovered period lies inside [6, 24] px. Grazing ground planes and far background are the cases that break this.

criteria.title: The screen on the character is object-locked
criteria.why: "you want those to track along with the character ... otherwise he'll appear to be swimming through a pattern" - Marco Recuay, research SS1.4.
criteria.check: Phase-correlate the band-passed lattice inside the character ROI between consecutive frames and divide by the character's own content displacement. Object-locked gives a ratio near 1; screen-locked gives a ratio near 0.

criteria.title: The screen on light is screen-locked
criteria.why: "Other times, you want them to be a little looser, so they feel like lights and not a texture" - Marco Recuay, research SS1.4; glows and flares carry a second, screen-locked screen, research SS1.7.
criteria.check: Phase-correlate the band-passed lattice inside glow/bloom regions between consecutive frames while the frame content moves by at least 2 px. A screen-locked screen does not move.

criteria.title: Dark bands carry lines, bright bands carry dots
criteria.why: "the thresher could be set to apply dots to the two brightest sections, and hatch lines to the two darker sections" - US 11270474, research SS1.6, SS2.2.
criteria.check: Spectral anisotropy per tone bin: a dot lattice has two orthogonal peaks of comparable magnitude (axis ratio ~0.7-1.0), a line screen has one (axis ratio < 0.4). The value is midBandAxisRatio minus darkBandAxisRatio; the detail carries both.

criteria.title: Hatch weight runs thick to thin with tone
criteria.why: "We'd combine line work, thick to thin, to get an overall value" - Danny Dimian, research SS2.2; width/pitch should run 0.15 at the light end to 0.55 at the dark end, research SS2.3.
criteria.check: Per dark-band tile, stroke width from component area divided by component length, normalised by the recovered pitch; correlated against (1 - mean luma) across tiles. The detail carries the observed width/pitch range, which should span at least 0.18-0.50.

criteria.title: Hatch pitch 7-11 px
criteria.why: research SS2.3 [EST]. See scaling.derivations - the research range is quoted at a 1080 p picture height; 7-8 px is where the brief and the scaled research overlap.
criteria.check: Median recovered period over tiles classified as line screens (axis ratio < 0.45).

criteria.title: Primary hatch angle 30-45 deg from horizontal
criteria.why: research SS2.3 [EST]; Hatcher exposes orientation per material and the artist dials it, research SS1.7.
criteria.check: Dominant spectral bearing of line-screen tiles, folded into 0-90 deg.

criteria.title: Cross-hatch second angle is +60 to +90 deg, and only in the darkest band
criteria.why: "cross-hatch second angle: first angle + 60 to 90 deg (not 90 exactly; 90 reads mechanical)" and "deepest shadow: add the second hatch direction only in the darkest band" - research SS2.3.
criteria.check: In the darkest tone quintile, the angular separation between the two strongest spectral axes.

criteria.title: Hatching concentrates at the terminator
criteria.why: Hatching lives in a Thresher band transition, so it naturally piles up at the lit/shadow boundary - "exactly where a comic inker puts it" - research SS2.2.
criteria.check: Mean hatch-mask density inside the top decile of |grad| of the low-passed luma, divided by the mean hatch density over the whole frame.

criteria.title: 30-75 % of pixels are exactly flat
criteria.why: "30-75 % of a typical region is exactly flat. That is enormously higher than a smooth-shaded render and is the strongest single signature of the look" - research SS5.3 [MEAS].
criteria.check: Median-filter the luma, then count the fraction of pixels with |grad luma| < 0.004.

criteria.title: 3-5 bands per material, with art-directed (uneven) spacing
criteria.why: The patent's worked example uses four luminance sections; research SS5.3 recommends 3-5 per material with band edges art-directed rather than evenly spaced, which is what makes a shadow shape designable rather than physical (SS5.4).
criteria.check: Segment the frame into hue/saturation regions, cluster plateau luma inside each sizeable region, take the median cluster count. The detail carries the coefficient of variation of the step sizes, which must be >= 0.15 - an evenly spaced toon ramp scores near 0.

criteria.title: Luma steps between plateaux are 0.08-0.20
criteria.why: "Per material there are only a handful of large tone breaks - luma steps of 0.08 to 0.20 - separating those plateaux" - research SS5.3 [MEAS].
criteria.check: Cluster plateau luma at 1/256 resolution, take the differences between adjacent significant clusters, report the median.

criteria.title: No smooth gradients survive
criteria.why: "We would have stepped values to avoid smooth grads" - Danny Dimian; "soft gradations are avoided in favor of halftoning and line hatching" - Imageworks, research SS5.1.
criteria.check: Fraction of pixels sitting inside a monotone luma ramp at least 24 px long whose per-pixel slope is in [0.0008, 0.004] - the signature of a surviving soft falloff.

criteria.title: Quantise first, then dither the step - band edges are screened, not hard contours
criteria.why: "a smooth gradient image is processed ... by quantizing ... and integrating the patterns generated by the hatcher in the transitions between gradient bands" - US 11270474, research SS1.1. Overlaying halftone on a smooth render gives texture but not the graphic read (SS5.1).
criteria.check: Locate band-transition pixels (between two plateau levels) and test each for lattice energy in its local spectrum. The value is the fraction of band-edge length that is screened rather than a clean contour.

criteria.title: Normal quantisation produces designed, faceted shadow shapes
criteria.why: "Quantising the normal rather than the shade is the key trick for designed shadows: it forces curved surfaces to read as a small number of flat facets, so the terminator lands on a designed edge instead of wandering smoothly" - research SS5.4, US 12293452.
criteria.check: Trace terminator contours and measure the fraction of contour length whose local tangent lies within 3 deg of one of at most 8 dominant orientations. A physically shaded curved surface scores low; a faceted one scores high.

criteria.title: Ink lines are coloured, never black
criteria.why: "the soft color line of 2D animation, making it any color the animator wanted" - Keyframe, research SS3.6; the one measured line was a desaturated teal #477373, not black.
criteria.check: Detect thin dark structures against a wide-radius background, then measure their chroma (max RGB - min RGB) and value. The value is the fraction of ink pixels with chroma >= 0.10; the detail carries median ink chroma, median ink luma (must be >= 0.10) and the ink hue clusters.

criteria.title: Ink line width is 5.3 px at our frame width
criteria.why: 5-6 px measured at 2000 px frame width on the ITSV Gwen still, research SS3.6 [MEAS]; x 1920/2000 = 4.8-5.8 px for us.
criteria.check: Per ink component, width = area / length from second moments; report the median across components.

criteria.title: Lines overshoot past silhouettes
criteria.why: "Miguel O'Hara: lines overshooting past his shoulder silhouette"; "a lot of line work overshooting from the surface" - research SS3.2, SS9.4. Overshoot is a recurring, nameable feature.
criteria.check: Find stroke endpoints from component second moments and test the underlying wide-radius luma gradient there. An endpoint sitting in flat territory means the line ran past the edge it described.

criteria.title: Lines boil on a held redraw interval
criteria.why: "one line set erasing off while the next draws on ... that crossfade is the mechanism behind the characteristic ink boil" - research SS3.3, SS3.5. redrawInterval is clamped to 1-4 frames.
criteria.check: Temporal step detection on the ink mask alone: the dominant update interval of the ink layer, measured the same way as the character pose rate.

criteria.title: Thick-thin taper along the stroke
criteria.why: "they could play with a thick-thin ... those sliders become a preset" - Gnomon panel, research SS3.4; weight varies along the stroke, SS3.6.
criteria.check: Ratio of the 90th to the 10th percentile of measured stroke width. A constant-width contour shader scores near 1.0.

criteria.title: Crease and construction lines, not only silhouette contours
criteria.why: "inklines are curves in 3D space and ... we use them a lot on face and hands"; The Spot literally carries construction lines inside him - research SS3.1, SS3.2.
criteria.check: Fraction of ink length whose underlying wide-radius luma gradient is weak and which is not adjacent to the subject's outer silhouette - i.e. interior detail lines.

criteria.title: Per-character / per-material line-style presets exist in code
criteria.why: "those sliders become a preset, and then those presets get saved for a character" - Gnomon panel, research SS3.4; ITSV/ATSV gave every character its own line logic (SS3.2). The system must not be a single global toon contour - the patent rejects rule-based toon shading outright (SS3.1).
criteria.check: Source: a named ink-style preset table with at least two distinct entries, and inkWeight / inkTint present in the look material parameters rather than a global screen-space edge filter.

criteria.title: Recombination is subtractive (CMY), not additive (RGB)
criteria.why: ATSV built a CMYK separator and a PigmentMerge node for "subtractive colour compositing to avoid an additive bias toward white" - research SS4.3.
criteria.check: At fringe pixels, the mean luma minus the flank-to-flank interpolated baseline. Additive recombination pushes overlaps toward white and yields a positive delta; subtractive keeps it at or below zero.

criteria.title: Per-separation offset ratios R:G:B = 0 : 1.0 : 0.45
criteria.why: "G displacement relative to R: +4 to +5 px", "B displacement relative to R: approx +2 px, i.e. B sits between R and G, nearer R" - research SS4.2 [MEAS]; the shader in SS4.3 uses 0.00 / 1.00 / 0.45.
criteria.check: Per-tile sub-pixel phase correlation of G against R and B against R (validated against synthetic shifts in score-selftest.mjs). The value is median|dB| / median|dG|; the detail carries the R-B-G ordering fraction, which must be >= 0.6.

criteria.title: Non-zero offset floor at the focal plane, about 1 px
criteria.why: "in-focus edges still fringe (median 0.15, up to 0.21 on the cup rim) ... Treat the offset as having a non-zero floor at the focal plane plus a depth-driven term" - research SS4.2; uFloorPx ~ 1.0 in SS4.3.
criteria.check: 10th percentile of per-tile |dG| across the frame, over tiles with enough structure to correlate.

criteria.title: Far field reaches 4-7.5 px of separation spread
criteria.why: "Total 3-channel spread approx 5 px at 803 px picture height" - research SS4.2 [MEAS]; SS4.3 tunes uDepthGain so the far background reaches 6-7 px at a 1080 p picture height, which is 4.5-5.2 px at ours.
criteria.check: 95th percentile of per-tile |dG| across the frame.

criteria.title: No gaussian blur anywhere in the frame
criteria.why: "It isn't a blur. It isn't out of focus. It's an image with different colors offset based on z-depth"; "Avoiding softness in the film meant avoiding using a traditional lens blur" - research SS4.1.
criteria.check: Radially averaged power spectra per tile; fit log(P_soft / P_sharpest) = -4 pi^2 sigma^2 f^2 over 0.06-0.40 cyc/px to recover an implied gaussian sigma. A channel offset is all-pass in magnitude and recovers sigma near 0; a real DOF blur does not. Guarded so genuinely flat tiles cannot register.

criteria.title: Cyan fringe on one flank, magenta on the other
criteria.why: "Fringe on the leading flank: cyan (G high, R low), peak R-G = -0.26. Fringe on the trailing flank: magenta (R high, G low), peak R-G = +0.23" - research SS4.2 [MEAS].
criteria.check: For each strong edge, the sign of the R-G excursion on each flank; the value is the fraction of edges whose two flanks carry opposite signs.

criteria.title: Offsets capped at 1 % of picture height
criteria.why: "very large offsets stop reading as print and start reading as an anaglyph. I would cap at roughly 1 % of picture height" - research SS4.4. 1 % of 803 px = 8.03 px.
criteria.check: Maximum per-tile |dG| over the whole frame set, allowing a small slack above the 8.03 px cap for measurement noise.

criteria.title: Fringing scales with defocus (about 5x per unit contrast)
criteria.why: "per unit of edge contrast the defocused fringing is about 5x stronger, and spatially about twice as wide" - research SS4.2 [MEAS], n=11 edges, uncertainty +/- 2x.
criteria.check: Fringe magnitude per unit edge contrast in opponent coordinates, computed separately for tiles in the low-offset (in-focus) and high-offset (defocused) populations; the value is the ratio. The detail carries the in-focus absolute value, which should land near 0.15.

criteria.title: No photographic motion blur on the fastest frames
criteria.why: "we tried not to have anything blurry" - Dimian; the film expresses motion as chromatic trailing, not blur - research SS6.5.
criteria.check: High-frequency energy ratio on the fastest frames divided by the same measure on the slowest frames. Real motion blur collapses the high band on fast frames.

criteria.title: Chromatic trailing appears where the frame is moving fast
criteria.why: "ChromaShifter ... on ATSV it was repurposed with motion vectors instead of depth to make motion trails" - research SS4.1, SS6.5.
criteria.check: Median per-tile |dG| restricted to tiles whose frame-to-frame content displacement is in the top quartile, on the fast shots.

criteria.title: The trail runs along the motion vector
criteria.why: The offset direction is the motion direction, not a fixed screen axis - research SS6.5 shader `motionTrail`.
criteria.check: Fraction of high-motion tiles whose channel-offset direction is within 30 deg of the tile's own content-motion direction.

criteria.title: The trail uses the same subtractive separation ratios as the defocus
criteria.why: `motionTrail` in research SS6.5 reuses 0.00 / 1.00 / 0.45 and the subtractive merge - motion and depth are the same operator with different drivers.
criteria.check: median|dB| / median|dG| restricted to high-motion tiles.

criteria.title: The character updates every 2 master frames
criteria.why: "on twos" means the pose is held for 2 frames of a 24 fps master - research SS6.1; beats.js STEP_SETS.ant = { step: 2, phase: 0 }.
criteria.check: Per-region pixel-difference timeline on the character ROI. For each candidate step and phase, the ratio of mean update-pair difference to mean hold-pair difference; the winning step must reach a contrast of at least 2.5. The detail carries the hold fraction, which must land in 0.35-0.62.

criteria.title: The camera updates every frame
criteria.why: beats.js STEP_SETS.camera = { step: 1, phase: 0 }; a character on 2s next to a camera on 1s is the effect - research SS6.3.
criteria.check: The same step detector on a background ROI, which is driven only by camera movement. No step >= 2 may reach a contrast of 2.5, and the background hold fraction must be <= 0.08.

criteria.title: At least three distinct per-part rates are in play
criteria.why: "different frame rates for different parts of his body at the same time - his body might be on twos and threes, his jacket would be on fours, his guitar would be on sixes" - Alan Hawkins, research SS6.2.
criteria.check: Edit: count the distinct `step` values declared in beats.js STEP_SETS.

criteria.title: Partition phases are offset so nothing pops in unison
criteria.why: "Offset the phase between partitions. If body-on-twos and jacket-on-fours both update on even frames, the character reads as one stepped object rather than several" - research SS6.4.
criteria.check: Edit: count the distinct `phase` values declared in beats.js STEP_SETS; at least two are required, and the antennae partition must not share both step and phase with the body.

criteria.title: The hero drops to 1s for the fastest action
criteria.why: A character on twos beside one on ones is a real and striking effect and is used as a differentiator - research SS6.3; beats.js ANT_ONES_RANGES covers the slam (138-158) and the swerve/vault (166-196).
criteria.check: The same step detector on the character ROI, restricted to the declared ones ranges; no step >= 2 may reach a contrast of 2.5 there.

criteria.title: The 2D FX layer is on 2s
criteria.why: "Everything in here updates on 2s (STEP_SETS.fx2d), never on 1s" - INTERFACES.md; hand-drawn FX on 2s, research SS8.
criteria.check: The step detector run on the FX-dominated regions of the frame (the residual after removing the slow-changing plate) during the FX beats.

criteria.title: Physics and secondary motion do not integrate through the holds
criteria.why: "Do not let the physics integrate through the hold. Either step the sim at the same rate or freeze it during the hold" - research SS6.4; ATSV needed a whole tool (Step sets) for exactly this - SS6.1.
criteria.check: Mean character-ROI difference across hold pairs divided by the mean across update pairs. Cloth, hair or antenna sims that keep integrating leak a visible residual into the holds.

criteria.title: Anticipation precedes every major action
criteria.why: Stylised timing is the reason for the stepping in the first place - the poses have to be worth holding. Research SS6.5 on smears and multiples assumes classical timing underneath.
criteria.check: At each major action beat taken from beats.js (FX_BEATS anchors and the shot starts), test whether the subject centroid moves counter to the subsequent action for at least 2 frames beforehand. The value is the count of beats showing anticipation.

criteria.title: Overshoot and settle after the big moves
criteria.why: Same reasoning as ANIM-01; a held pose that arrives without overshoot reads as interpolation rather than acting.
criteria.check: Count of action beats where the subject centroid crosses its post-action resting value and returns within 6 frames.

criteria.title: Smears or multiples during the fastest action
criteria.why: "post stamp ... creates geometry duplicates so you can have like multiple limbs for smears" - research SS6.5; smears are how speed is expressed when motion blur is banned.
criteria.check: On the ones ranges, count frames where the subject silhouette's second-moment anisotropy spikes above 2x its running median or the subject's connected-component count jumps - both signatures of a smear or a multiple.

criteria.title: Real held frames with substantial pose changes between them
criteria.why: Holding is only worth doing if the change between holds is big; micro-jitter on 2s looks like a bug, not a choice - research SS6.1, SS6.4.
criteria.check: Overall character hold fraction across the film. The detail carries the median inter-pose difference, which must be >= 0.02 so the holds separate genuinely different poses.

criteria.title: Strong readable silhouettes
criteria.why: With flat bands and no soft falloff, the silhouette is doing nearly all the work of reading the pose - research SS5.1.
criteria.check: Mean luma-plus-chroma separation between the subject silhouette and the ring of background immediately outside it, averaged over the film.

criteria.title: Weight on the impact
criteria.why: beats.js shot E is the slam: flash, radial burst, KRAKOOM, shockwave, 3-panel split, channel tear - all of it has to be paid for with a motion-energy spike and a decay.
criteria.check: Peak whole-frame motion energy in frames 138-146 divided by the running median of the preceding shot, with the requirement that the energy then decays over at least 6 frames.

criteria.title: Motion is eased, not linear
criteria.why: Constant-velocity translation is the tell of an un-animated transform; the acting has to accelerate and decelerate.
criteria.check: Coefficient of variation of the per-frame subject centroid speed within each shot, averaged over shots.

criteria.title: Bold pop-art saturation
criteria.why: The look is "clean, colourful, stylised" comic print; research SS7.1 has colour "completely replacing the colour wholesale" to hit a scripted distribution.
criteria.check: Mean HSV saturation over the film; the detail carries the fraction of pixels above S = 0.5, which must be >= 0.28.

criteria.title: Flat colour dominates the frame
criteria.why: Print is flat ink. If the top few colours do not cover most of the frame you are still looking at a shaded render - research SS5.1, SS5.3.
criteria.check: Coverage of the 16 most common 5-bit-quantised colours; the detail carries the count of distinct 5-bit colours, which must be <= 6000.

criteria.title: Every shot has its own colour script
criteria.why: "colour was carefully scripted in by the art directors ... completely replacing the colour wholesale, so that we can get the specific distributions of colours in frames" - research SS7.1; beats.js gives four worlds (tabletop, eclipse, impact, payoff).
criteria.check: Median angular distance between the dominant hues of consecutive shots, measured on each shot's mid-point frame.

criteria.title: Complementary opposition inside the frame
criteria.why: Pop-art comic colour works by putting near-opposite hues against each other; the misregistration fringes are themselves cyan/magenta opposites - research SS4.2, SS7.3.
criteria.check: Take the mass-weighted top hue clusters and score the best pair by how close their separation is to 180 deg, weighted by their combined mass.

criteria.title: Band colours come from a palette LUT, not from shaded albedo
criteria.why: "quantise luminance into bands, then look up each band's colour from a per-shot, per-world palette rather than from the albedo" - research SS7.1 `paletteShade`.
criteria.check: Within each material region, measure the hue drift between the brightest and darkest plateau. A pure luminance scaling of one albedo holds hue constant; a palette LUT shifts it.

criteria.title: Background simplifies with depth
criteria.why: "scenes are selectively simplified - so as you go into the background here, detail is falling away - and we're applying all the printing techniques ... in order to support art direction" - research SS7.2.
criteria.check: High-frequency detail density in the far band of the frame divided by the density in the near band, where far/near is estimated from the per-tile misregistration magnitude. The detail also reports that per-tile offset rises with far-ness (correlation >= 0.25).

criteria.title: Paper-white and non-neutral deep-shadow anchors both present
criteria.why: research SS7.3 gives every world a paper/highlight value and a deep shadow value, and neither is neutral - #1A0B2E, not #000000.
criteria.check: Presence and coverage of a near-paper cluster (L >= 0.88, S <= 0.12, coverage 0.01-0.35) and of a deep cluster (L <= 0.16, coverage 0.02-0.35) whose chroma is >= 0.04. The value is the fraction of the two conditions met, averaged over frames.

criteria.title: Shadow shapes are designed, not physical
criteria.why: "you are choosing a luminance threshold, so the shadow's shape is the iso-contour of the lighting at that threshold. To get shapes that are genuinely designed ... room shaders ... quantization of surface normals" - research SS5.4.
criteria.check: Shadow-region boundaries have few dominant tangent orientations and each shadow region is a large graphic shape: the value combines the terminator facet fraction with the requirement that the largest shadow region covers at least 2 % of the frame.

criteria.title: Rim light carries halftone
criteria.why: "the halftone dots you see in rim lights on a character" - Marco Recuay, research SS1.4; "Halftone dots were sprinkled to represent the glows" - Geeta Basantani, SS1.7.
criteria.check: Identify thin bright bands running along subject silhouettes, then measure the band-passed lattice signal-to-noise inside them.

criteria.title: Flares are graphic and hard-edged, not anamorphic
criteria.why: "flare as drawn shape, not as optical artifact. That argues against an anamorphic streak model" - research SS8, SS10.2; "the flares had halftones which scaled with light" - SS1.7.
criteria.check: For detected flare elements (bright, saturated, high-contrast against their surround), the 10-90 % edge transition width in px; the detail rejects any flare whose bounding aspect ratio exceeds 6:1 with a horizontal major axis.

criteria.title: Glow dots at a coarser, screen-locked pitch
criteria.why: "run a second, independent screen on your bloom/glow buffer, screen-locked, coarser pitch, with the multiplier biased above 1.0" - research SS1.7; SS1.8 gives 16-21 px at a 1080 p picture height = 11.9-15.6 px at ours.
criteria.check: Recovered period inside glow/bloom regions (brightest, low-gradient, high-value regions), which must be clearly coarser than the character screen.

criteria.title: The tumbler actually eclipses the key light
criteria.why: beats.js shot D: "The tumbler descends and eclipses the window light." If the key does not fall, the eclipse is decoration rather than lighting.
criteria.check: Relative drop in frame mean luma between the start and the darkest point of shot D.

criteria.title: Impact flash at the slam
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS has impactFlash at 138-144; a slam without a luminance event does not land.
criteria.check: Peak frame mean luma in 138-146 divided by the mean over the preceding 8 frames, with the spike lasting no more than 4 frames.

criteria.title: Speed lines on the sprint, horizontally dominant
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: speedLines horizontal across 36-80; "Graphic elements - used to fill the frame" - research SS8.
criteria.check: Hough-style straight-line detection on the edge map; count of long thin strokes, with the detail requiring at least 60 % of them within 20 deg of the declared direction.

criteria.title: Radial speed lines converge on their anchor
criteria.why: beats.js declares radial speedLines at 84-114 and 160-176; radial lines only read if they actually share a vanishing point.
criteria.check: Fraction of detected lines whose infinite extension passes within 12 % of frame width of the best-fit common point.

criteria.title: Impact burst at the slam
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: radialBurst 138-152 at scale 1.5, plus the earlier burst at 24-34 and the payoff burst at 228-240.
criteria.check: Count of radial ray or wedge elements emanating from the burst anchor, measured as angular spokes in the polar transform about that anchor.

criteria.title: Kirby-style crackle
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: crackle 118-140 - the jagged angular energy shapes of the comic idiom, drawn not simulated.
criteria.check: Count of high-contrast closed or branching polygons with a high vertex turn rate (jagged, not smooth) inside the crackle region.

criteria.title: Sparkles on the payoff
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: sparkle 220-240 over the grab.
criteria.check: Count of small bright elements with four-point star symmetry (cross-correlation against a rotated cross template) in the payoff frames.

criteria.title: Zip ribbons following the ant
criteria.why: "Zip ribbons - ATSV motion graphic language ... ribbon geometry along motion paths, flat-shaded, on their own frame rate" - research SS8; beats.js zipRibbon 40-80 and arcRibbon 176-202.
criteria.check: Longest continuous elongated flat-filled element measured as a fraction of frame width; the detail requires it to trail the subject rather than sit static.

criteria.title: Debris spray from the impact
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: debrisSpray 140-168.
criteria.check: Count of small discrete high-contrast elements whose frame-to-frame displacement points away from the impact anchor.

criteria.title: Shock ring expands from the impact
criteria.why: beats.js FX_BEATS: shockRing 139-158; the ring has to grow or it is a decal.
criteria.check: Radial profile about the anchor per frame; the radius of the dominant annulus must increase monotonically. The value is the total growth in px.

criteria.title: Every 2D FX element animates on 2s
criteria.why: "Everything in here updates on 2s (STEP_SETS.fx2d), never on 1s" - INTERFACES.md; hand-drawn FX are drawn on 2s, research SS8.
criteria.check: Step detection on the FX residual layer (frame minus a temporally smoothed plate) during the FX beats.

criteria.title: Bold graphic shape language - flat fills, hard edges, palette hues
criteria.why: The FX are drawings, not renders: "Graphic elements used to fill the frame like BOOM and POW" - research SS8; nothing soft, SS5.1.
criteria.check: For detected FX elements: interior gradient magnitude (must be <= 0.02, i.e. flat fill), 10-90 % edge width (must be <= 2.0 px) and the count of distinct FX hues across the film (must be >= 3). The value is the fraction of those three conditions met.

criteria.title: Hand-lettered onomatopoeia on every declared beat
criteria.why: "Graphic elements - used to fill the frame like 'BOOM' and 'POW'" - fxguide, research SS8; beats.js LETTERING declares SKITT, SKITT, KRAKOOM, SKRRT, VWOOP and SNATCH.
criteria.check: At each LETTERING anchor and frame range, test for a large high-contrast closed-contour graphic cluster of roughly the declared scale. The value is the fraction of the six beats where lettering is found.

criteria.title: Multi-layer comic outline around the letterforms
criteria.why: "hand-drawn-style with heavy outlines" - research SS8.1; comic lettering is a fill plus at least one keyline plus a drop, never a bare glyph.
criteria.check: Radial colour profile outward from letter stroke cores; count the distinct concentric bands before reaching the plate. The detail carries stroke width / cap height, which must be >= 0.14 (heavy).

criteria.title: Per-letter rotation jitter
criteria.why: "per-letter rotation and baseline jitter - the genre convention descends from comic letterers using Speedball pens" - research SS8.1.
criteria.check: Standard deviation of the principal-axis angle across the letter components of one word.

criteria.title: Baseline jitter
criteria.why: research SS8.1, as above - a straight mechanical baseline is the tell of a font.
criteria.check: Standard deviation of letter-component centroid height, normalised by the measured cap height of the word.

criteria.title: Pop-in on 2s with an overshoot
criteria.why: beats.js: "Held on the beat, animated on 2s, with a pop-in overshoot and a hold"; FX and lettering share the 2s rule, research SS8.
criteria.check: Step detection on the lettering ROI over the first 8 frames of each word, plus the scale timeline, which must exceed its settled size by at least 8 % before settling.

criteria.title: Letterforms are original vectors, with no font files anywhere
criteria.why: "the practical route is an SDF atlas of hand-drawn glyphs ... rather than a font file, because the expressive distortion is the point" - research SS8.1; INTERFACES.md: "Original vector letterforms, authored in this repo. No font files, no downloaded assets."
criteria.check: Source: no .ttf/.otf/.woff/.woff2 files anywhere under spiderverse/, and app/scene/letters.js exports getGlyph and layoutWord.

criteria.title: Comic panel borders are present on the declared panel beats
criteria.why: "Panelization - breaks up action into panels" - fxguide, research SS8, SS10.3; beats.js PANELS declares a caption panel, a 3-way split and a hero panel.
criteria.check: For each declared panel rect, sample the border path and measure the mean gradient magnitude across it relative to the frame mean. The value is the fraction of declared panel beats where a border is detected.

criteria.title: The 3-panel split at the slam sits where the edit says
criteria.why: beats.js PANELS split3 at 140-158 with rects at x = 0-0.36, 0.37-0.66, 0.67-1.0; gutters of 0.8-1.2 % of picture width read correctly - research SS10.3.
criteria.check: Recover the internal vertical gutter positions from column-wise gradient peaks and compare with the declared rects. The value is the largest positional error in px; the detail checks that the gutter widths fall in 0.8-1.2 % of frame width (15-23 px).

criteria.title: Each panel in the split shows a genuinely different camera
criteria.why: beats.js supplies three distinct camOffsets and lenses for the split; three copies of the same angle is a gradient, not a panel split - research SS10.3 renders N virtual cameras into an atlas.
criteria.check: Normalised cross-correlation between the contents of each pair of panels, scaled to a common size. The value is the highest pairwise correlation.

criteria.title: Freeze frames genuinely hold the beauty
criteria.why: beats.js FREEZES holds frames 24-30 from source 24 and 228-240 from source 228; sourceFrame() says the geometry evaluated is the source frame.
criteria.check: Mean absolute difference of the low-passed (content) image between consecutive frames inside each freeze range.

criteria.title: Screens, grain and FX keep running over the frozen beauty
criteria.why: "a frozen panel is just a frozen input texture - the screens and grain should keep running over it or it will look like a still image pasted in" - research SS10.3.
criteria.check: Mean absolute difference of the high-passed image between consecutive frames inside each freeze range, which must stay clearly non-zero while PANEL-04 holds.

criteria.title: Caption boxes on the caption beats
criteria.why: "Thought bubbles / caption boxes - ATSV uses both ... screen-space UI layer, composited before paper grain" - research SS8; beats.js declares 'ONE CRUMB.' at 26 and 'CRUMB.' at 231.
criteria.check: Detect a rectangular high-contrast bordered region containing lettering, appearing at the declared captionIn frames. The value is the fraction of declared captions found.

criteria.title: Layer tearing - horizontal band displacement
criteria.why: "Glitch artifacts - The Spot / Miles' glitching ... horizontal band displacement + channel separation + scanline drop" - research SS8; beats.js glitchTear at 130-136 and 141-147.
criteria.check: Per-row horizontal displacement estimated against the previous frame; count rows whose displacement differs from their neighbours by more than 4 px. The value is the largest such row-to-row displacement discontinuity in px.

criteria.title: Channel splitting spikes during the glitch
criteria.why: Same source as GLITCH-01; the glitch is a deliberate exaggeration of the misregistration the whole film already runs on - research SS8, SS4.
criteria.check: Median per-tile |dG| on the glitch frames divided by the median on the surrounding non-glitch frames of the same shot.

criteria.title: A brief shift into another universe's art style, which then reverts
criteria.why: Each universe gets its own quantisation, line style, palette and frame-rate rules - research SS9; beats.js styleBreak 'graphite' at 176-184. Brief is the point: it must revert.
criteria.check: Composite style-vector distance (pitch, band count, saturation, ink chroma, plateau fraction) between the style-break frames and the shot's baseline, plus the requirement that the vector returns inside tolerance within 6 frames of the break ending.

criteria.title: The style break reads as a coherent other medium, not as a bug
criteria.why: Vulture is "sketchy quill pen strokes on old worn parchment"; Hobie is screen-print cut-out; the graphite break has to be as internally consistent as those - research SS9.3, SS9.6.
criteria.check: Human verdict recorded in verdicts.json against the rendered 176-184 range: the break must read as a deliberate alternate art style with its own line, tone and palette logic.

criteria.title: Paper grain at 2-4 % amplitude
criteria.why: "low-amplitude static noise, locked to the frame not the camera, ~2-4 % amplitude, multiply" - research SS8.
criteria.check: RMS of (luma - 3x3 median) restricted to plateau interiors, so real detail cannot inflate it.

criteria.title: Grain is frame-locked, not camera-locked
criteria.why: "Paper grain that tracks the camera reads as texture on the world; grain locked to the frame reads as the page the world is printed on. That single distinction does a lot of work" - research Appendix D.
criteria.check: Phase-correlate the grain residual between consecutive frames and, separately, the low-passed content. The value is the grain's best-fit shift; it is only evaluated on frame pairs where the content itself moved by at least 2 px.

criteria.title: Grain sits over everything, dark bands included
criteria.why: Grain is the last pass in the graph and applies to the finished page - research Appendix D step 12. Grain that only appears in the mid-tones means it was applied before something else.
criteria.check: Grain RMS in the darkest tone tercile divided by grain RMS in the brightest tercile.

criteria.title: Grain is at output resolution and has print texture, not flat white noise
criteria.why: "grain last, grain at output res" - research Appendix D; the texture is paper fibre, which has spectral structure, not a flat noise floor. Vulture is literally "on old worn parchment" - SS9.6.
criteria.check: Fraction of the grain residual's spectral energy above 0.35 cyc/px (proving it was generated at output resolution rather than upscaled), with the detail reporting the spectral slope, which must be in [-1.2, -0.05] - structured, not flat.

criteria.title: A modest vignette
criteria.why: "Vignette - not documented specifically ... modest" - research SS8 [EST].
criteria.check: 1 - (mean luma of the corner regions / mean luma of the central region), averaged over the film.

criteria.title: The vignette is applied before the screen, so the dots vignette too
criteria.why: "apply it before the screen so the dots vignette too" - research SS8.
criteria.check: Dot coverage (dot-mask area fraction) in the corner tiles divided by dot coverage in the central tiles. An upstream vignette pushes the corners into darker bands and grows their dots; a downstream vignette leaves the dot geometry untouched.

criteria.title: 2.39:1 at 1920 x 803
criteria.why: "Aspect ratio 2.39:1" confirmed on unletterboxed stills - research SS10.2 [MEAS]; beats.js OUT_WIDTH/OUT_HEIGHT.
criteria.check: Decoded PNG dimensions and their ratio, on every frame.

criteria.title: Wide lenses throughout
criteria.why: "Very wide lenses are used, and they break the screen projection" - the Hatcher patent notes tri-planar failure "when a camera is very wide", which tells you wide framing was common enough to drive a tool feature - research SS10.2. beats.js declares 16-28 mm.
criteria.check: Edit: every shot's declared lens must be inside 14-30 mm equivalent. The value is the widest declared lens; the detail lists all seven.

criteria.title: Dutch angles on every shot
criteria.why: "Dutch angles and whip pans are conventional camera animation" in this idiom - research SS10.3; beats.js gives every shot a non-zero dutch from -14 to +11 deg.
criteria.check: Edit: the smallest |dutch| across the seven shots. The detail carries a pixel-side confirmation - the dominant straight-edge orientation in the plate must be off-axis by at least 1.5 deg.

criteria.title: The camera moves purposefully in every shot
criteria.why: A locked-off camera cannot be on 1s against a character on 2s, which is the effect the whole stepping scheme exists to produce - research SS6.3.
criteria.check: Median per-frame global content displacement within each shot, excluding freeze ranges; the value is the smallest such median across the seven shots.

criteria.title: Whip transitions at the cuts
criteria.why: "a whip pan should express itself through chromatic trailing rather than motion blur" - research SS10.3; beats.js fires a cutWhip audio cue at 36, 80, 114, 158 and 202.
criteria.check: Global motion energy in the 3 frames either side of each cut divided by the shot's median. The value is the smallest ratio across the six cuts.

criteria.title: The camera takes the weight of the impact
criteria.why: beats.js shot E is the slam with subDrop and glassRing; the camera has to react and then recover.
criteria.check: Frame-to-frame global displacement after frame 138 must show an oscillation whose envelope decays monotonically; the value is the number of frames over which it decays.

criteria.title: The freeze-frame panel moments are genuine camera holds
criteria.why: beats.js FREEZES at 24-30 and 228-240; a freeze with a drifting camera is a slow-motion shot, not a panel.
criteria.check: Global content displacement between consecutive frames inside the freeze ranges.

criteria.title: MRT G-buffer with the lighting term separated from beauty
criteria.why: "Separating luma from beauty is the single most important choice. The Thresher quantises a luminance gradient and re-applies it as a multiply, so you need the lighting term independent of albedo or you will band the texture detail instead of the light" - research SS Architecture, Appendix D step 1.
criteria.check: Source: the renderer declares at least four colour attachments and a lumaLighting channel distinct from beauty, per INTERFACES.md's G-buffer table.

criteria.title: Quantise before you dither
criteria.why: Appendix D steps 4 then 5: Thresher banding, then Hatcher screens. "A common mistake is to overlay halftone on a smooth render, which gives you texture but not the graphic read" - research SS5.1.
criteria.check: Source: in the declared PASS_ORDER list, the Thresher banding pass must appear before the Hatcher screen pass.

criteria.title: The screen is applied with a multiply, never an over or an overlay
criteria.why: "Step 6 must be a multiply, not an over. The whole point of the patent's multiplier layer is that the screen modulates whatever is underneath and can exceed 1.0 to brighten" - research Appendix D.
criteria.check: Source: the screen application pass must be a multiply against the beauty (PRINT-08 measures the same thing from pixels), and must not use an over/overlay/screen blend for the screentone.

criteria.title: The palette map runs after the multiply
criteria.why: Appendix D steps 6 then 7 - the band index selects a scripted colour after the screen has decided which band the pixel is in, research SS7.1.
criteria.check: Source: in PASS_ORDER, screenMultiply must appear before paletteMap.

criteria.title: Screens before misregistration
criteria.why: Appendix D steps 5-6 then 9. Misregistering first and then screening would put a single clean screen over already-split separations and destroy the fringe colours measured in SS4.2.
criteria.check: Source: in PASS_ORDER, screenMultiply must appear before misregistration.

criteria.title: Panels, graphics and type composite after misregistration and before grain
criteria.why: Appendix D step 11 sits between misregistration (9-10) and grain (12); caption boxes are "composited before paper grain" - research SS8.
criteria.check: Source: in PASS_ORDER, misregistration appears before the panels/graphics/type pass, which appears before the grain pass.

criteria.title: Grain and vignette last, at output resolution
criteria.why: "grain last, grain at output res" and "Step 12 is frame-locked, not camera-locked" - research Appendix D.
criteria.check: Source: grain is the final entry of PASS_ORDER before the output transform, and is evaluated after any supersample downsample.

criteria.title: Shot A reads as the sighting
criteria.why: beats.js A: "Extreme low wide. Ant crests the sugar packet ridge, spots the crumb across the table." A sighting needs a small subject and a legible distant target.
criteria.check: Subject silhouette area as a fraction of the frame, averaged over shot A. The detail confirms a separate high-contrast element exists in the upper half (the crumb across the table) and that the subject centroid sits below the frame's vertical midpoint (low camera).

criteria.title: Shot B reads as a sprint
criteria.why: beats.js B: "Side-on truck. Ant sprints left to right, legs on 2s with smears, camera on 1s."
criteria.check: Horizontal traverse of the subject centroid across shot B as a fraction of frame width, signed left to right. The detail requires the dominant global motion to be horizontal on at least 75 % of frames.

criteria.title: Shot C reads as a charge into the lens with a shadow sweep
criteria.why: beats.js C: "Ant charges the lens. A shadow sweeps over; it looks up."
criteria.check: Ratio of the subject silhouette area in the last quarter of shot C to the first quarter. The detail requires a mid-shot mean-luma dip of at least 15 % (the shadow sweeping over).

criteria.title: Shot D - the cup descends and eclipses the light
criteria.why: beats.js D: "Up-angle hero. The tumbler descends and eclipses the window light. Crackle rim."
criteria.check: Vertical travel of the centroid of the largest dark region across shot D, as a fraction of picture height, with the requirement that it moves downward. LIGHT-05 measures the luminance consequence separately.

criteria.title: Shot E lands as an impact
criteria.why: beats.js E: "Impact. Flash, radial burst, KRAKOOM, shockwave, 3-panel split, channel tear." All five devices are separately scored; this one asks whether the composite event actually reads.
criteria.check: Composite impact score over 138-158: the fraction of the five declared devices (flash, burst, shock ring, panel split, channel tear/glitch) that are detected inside their declared windows.

criteria.title: Shot F reads as a swerve and a vault
criteria.why: beats.js F: "Drift, plant, run the curved glass, kick off the rim in a graphic arc. Style break mid-vault."
criteria.check: Total heading change of the subject centroid path across shot F in degrees. The detail requires the centroid to rise by at least 12 % of picture height during 176-202 (the vault leaves the ground).

criteria.title: Shot G lands the grab
criteria.why: beats.js G: "Land, slide, snatch the crumb, hero pose, freeze into a comic panel with title lockup." The grab only reads if the crumb and the ant converge and then travel together.
criteria.check: Track the subject and the secondary (crumb) element; after the declared snatch at frame 220 their motion vectors must correlate. The value is that post-grab motion correlation; the detail requires their separation to fall below 25 % of its shot-start value first.

criteria.title: Every cut changes the frame materially
criteria.why: Seven shots in ten seconds only works if each cut is a real change of size or angle; otherwise the edit reads as one long move with jump cuts.
criteria.check: Normalised cross-correlation between the last frame of each shot and the first frame of the next, downsampled. The value is the median across the six cuts.

criteria.title: Staging uses the frame - the subject is not parked in the middle
criteria.why: Comic composition is asymmetric and uses negative space for the lettering and FX that beats.js anchors off-centre.
criteria.check: Fraction of frames whose subject centroid sits within 8 % of the exact frame centre. The detail checks lead room on shot B - the subject must have more empty frame ahead of it than behind on at least 60 % of frames.

criteria.title: The ant has head, thorax, petiole and gaster as distinct articulated parts
criteria.why: Formicid anatomy is the whole reason the subject reads as an ant rather than a bug-shaped blob; the brief asks for more fine detail than the reference where technically possible.
criteria.check: Audit: app/scene/ant.js exposes named parts covering head, thorax, petiole and gaster, and all four move independently across the film.

criteria.title: Six legs, each with at least four segments
criteria.why: Coxa, femur, tibia, tarsus at minimum; a two-bone leg cannot make the gait read at macro scale.
criteria.check: Audit: ant.legs length is 6 and ant.legSegments is at least 4.

criteria.title: Segmented antennae with a scape and funiculus break
criteria.why: The elbowed antenna is the single most recognisable ant silhouette cue, and beats.js puts the antennae on their own frame rate (STEP_SETS.antennae, step 3, phase 1) so they must be independently articulated.
criteria.check: Audit: ant.antennaSegments is at least 6 per antenna.

criteria.title: Mandibles that actually articulate
criteria.why: The grab in shot G is played with the mandibles; static jaws make the payoff a collision rather than an action.
criteria.check: Audit: ant.mandibleOpenRange is greater than zero, and the pixel-side detail confirms the head silhouette changes shape around the declared snatch at frame 220.

criteria.title: Bristles and setae on the cuticle
criteria.why: At true macro scale (a 4 mm ant on a wide lens) setae are the surface detail that sells the scale; without them the shell reads as plastic.
criteria.check: Audit: ant.bristles count.

criteria.title: Nothing in the scene is a bare primitive
criteria.why: Repo-wide rule and the brief's explicit requirement. A BoxGeometry standing in for a prop is visible instantly under flat banding, because flat shading removes every other cue except shape.
criteria.check: Audit: scene.barePrimitives must be 0 - every geometry has been deformed, beveled, noised or CSG'd before it reaches the scene graph. The detail carries the ant triangle count, which must be at least 40000.

criteria.title: The set is dressed
criteria.why: A tabletop with one crumb on it is a turntable. The brief asks for a dressed set: sugar packet, tumbler, napkin, spoon, spill, crumbs, table grain, and whatever else the shot list needs.
criteria.check: Audit: scene.propCount - the number of distinct authored set-dressing objects, excluding the ant and instanced duplicates of the same prop.

criteria.title: The subject silhouette is spindly and legged, not a blob
criteria.why: This is the pixel-side cross-check on CRAFT-01 to CRAFT-05: an articulated insect has a high perimeter-to-area ratio, and a placeholder capsule does not.
criteria.check: Perimeter squared divided by area of the extracted subject silhouette, averaged over frames where the subject covers at least 0.5 % of the frame. A circle scores 12.6; a six-legged insect with antennae scores well above 45.

criteria.title: No Math.random anywhere in the production code
criteria.why: "No Math.random anywhere in scene or FX code. Use rng(seed) from app/core/prng.js; every frame must be reproducible or before/after comparison is meaningless" - INTERFACES.md; repo rule AGENTS.md architecture rule 4.
criteria.check: Source: grep for Math.random under spiderverse/app.

criteria.title: No downloaded or third-party image assets
criteria.why: Original or CC0 only, and in practice this production generates everything procedurally - a downloaded texture is both a licensing risk and a way to fake detail the renderer did not earn. GAUNTLET.md rule C1/C4.
criteria.check: Source: no raster image files under spiderverse/ outside spiderverse/out, and no image data URIs larger than 4 KB in app code.

criteria.title: No reference frames or third-party footage used as scenery
criteria.why: GAUNTLET.md rules C1 and C2 - reference material is for comparison only, never as content.
criteria.check: Source: no imports from reference/, no VideoTexture, no <video>/<iframe>, no .mp4, and no remote URLs in app code.

criteria.title: No wall-clock time and no network at render time
criteria.why: "All time-varying values take an explicit frame argument. Nothing reads a wall clock" - INTERFACES.md. A render that reads the clock or the network is not reproducible and the whole before/after loop collapses.
criteria.check: Source: grep for Date.now, performance.now, new Date(, fetch(, XMLHttpRequest under spiderverse/app.

criteria.title: Renders are deterministic to the byte
criteria.why: GAUNTLET.md rule B5 - a flaky render can hide regressions behind noise, and every measurement in this rubric assumes the frame is reproducible.
criteria.check: Render a sample of frames a second time into spiderverse/out/frames-verify and compare sha256 per file. The value is the number of mismatching frames.

criteria.title: The whole 240-frame render finishes inside 45 minutes
criteria.why: The iteration loop is the product. A render slower than this cannot be run often enough to converge, and the whole comp-chain architecture exists partly because it was applied "at the last stage possible ... to allow us to get as many iterations as possible" - research SS8.2.
criteria.check: spiderverse/out/render-stats.json totalSeconds.

criteria.title: All 240 frames exist at 1920 x 803
criteria.why: beats.js DURATION_FRAMES = 240 at OUT_WIDTH x OUT_HEIGHT; a short frame set means a criterion measured on a missing beat silently passes.
criteria.check: Count and decode every frame_%04d.png in the frames directory and verify its dimensions.
